scientific_question: Can all 208 accepted Hindsight requirement blocks be assigned to their uv.lock registries without changing or dropping any block byte?
decision_informed: Whether PyPI and PyTorch CPU wheel acquisitions can be isolated into source-faithful, hash-enforced routes.
scientific_evidence_role: Offline dependency-routing evidence only; no download, installation, model, lifecycle, numerical, superiority, or SOTA claim is eligible.

diagnosed_change_only.from: rely on uv --emit-index-url to serialize a package-level explicit source
diagnosed_change_only.to: derive a byte-traceable per-requirement route from the accepted dependency body and the two exact registries present in uv.lock
diagnosed_change_only.unchanged: source revision, uv.lock, accepted dependency body, versions, hashes, markers, ordering, Python platform, resources, and scientific roles

acceptance: Source, uv.lock, and accepted dependency-body identities match and the source remains clean.
uv.lock contains exactly the PyPI and official PyTorch CPU registries.
Two independent splits are identical and produce 206 PyPI blocks plus 2 torch blocks.
Every requirement block has one route, retained byte range and SHA-256, and the ordered manifest reconstructs all 256006 accepted bytes exactly.
The terminal evidence inventory verifies and accepted/rejected sentinels are mutually consistent.
failure: Any collision, identity change, registry-set change, cardinality change, malformed block, reconstruction mismatch, source mutation, or timeout seals the fresh root TERMINAL_REJECTED and preserves it.
next_gate_after_acceptance: Independently audit both routed requirement files, then freeze their sequential --no-deps --require-hashes --only-binary wheel acquisition. Do not download until Wave1 is terminally accepted and its services are released.
prohibited_actions: editing, deleting, or relabeling any earlier export evidence
changing, reordering, normalizing, dropping, or duplicating a requirement block
routing any non-torch dependency through the PyTorch index or torch through PyPI
downloading wheels, installing packages, downloading models, or starting a numerical run
